subject: Encryption stewardship: BYOK operator roles & network isolation RFC
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, ACME Security <sec-ops@acme.com>, Owen Park <owen@helioscloud.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Encryption stewardship: BYOK operator roles & network isolation RFC

Team / ACME / Helios –

Attached is a short RFC proposing how we want to partition responsibilities and network boundaries for BYOK/HSM operators in private deployments (VPC and on-prem). High-level goals: minimize operator blast radius, make rotations auditable and automatable, and guarantee no plaintext key material leaves customer boundary.

Key proposals (TL;DR):
- Operator role separation: distinct "Custody Operator" (physically authorized, HSM unseal) vs "Maintenance Operator" (software/admin ops). No single human holds both privileges.
- Ephemeral wrapping keys: HSM generates short-lived wrapping key; KMS stores wrapped CEKs only. Vault/Transit used for orchestration; wrapping performed inside tenant VPC or on-prem HSM.
- Network controls: dedicated management subnet for KMS/HSM control plane, strict ACLs, egress blocked except to monitored telemetry collectors over mTLS to Helios (if customer allows), and cross-region replication via encrypted tunnels only.
- Rotation automation: rotation triggered by schedule or event with staged rollout (staging -> canary -> global), automated snapshot and audit log ingestion to REDWOOD-OBS for replayable audit.
- Telemetry & audit: signed attestations from HSM, operator action timeline (who did what, via which KMS API key), and immutable evidence bundle stored in customer-controlled storage.

Action items:
1) ACME: confirm whether Helios-managed telemetry endpoints are acceptable or if they require on-prem collector.
2) Helios: provide the mTLS cert fingerprint and allowed IP ranges for the telemetry ingress.
3) Internal (Monica/Tessa): review attached operator-roles-matrix.xlsx and comment by EOD Fri; we'll iterate to final.

I've attached a short diagram and the operator matrix. I expect this RFC to drive the next SOC review and the SOC checklist we hand to customers.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: rfc-encryption-stewardship-v1.pdf, operator-roles-matrix.xlsx, network-segmentation-diagram.png

From: Owen Park <owen@helioscloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, ACME Security <sec-ops@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:02:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Encryption stewardship: BYOK operator roles & network isolation RFC

Ben / Monica –

Thanks for the RFC and the clear breakdown. A couple quick clarifying questions from Helios infra: 
1) For the ephemeral wrapping keys generated inside the HSM, do you expect Helios to host the private CA for mTLS to the telemetry collector, or would ACME prefer we accept customer-supplied certs?
2) You mention cross-region replication via encrypted tunnels. Do you anticipate that replication will require remote unseal keys on the standby region HSMs, or are you planning to replicate wrapped CEKs only and perform unseal locally?

From a compliance perspective, Helios prefers to avoid persistent private keys on standby nodes; wrapped CEK replication is ideal. We can support either model but need to know which to document in our runbooks.

Happy to hop on a 30m call to walk through the TLS and IP requirements.

—Owen
Owen Park
Principal Infra Engineer, Helios Cloud

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Owen Park <owen@helioscloud.com>, ACME Security <sec-ops@acme.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Encryption stewardship: BYOK operator roles & network isolation RFC

On Wed, Nov 18, 2026 at 9:15 AM Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / ACME / Helios –
> 
> Attached is a short RFC proposing how we want to partition responsibilities and network boundaries for BYOK/HSM operators in private deployments (VPC and on-prem).

Thanks, Ben. A few follow-ups inline and in the matrix (see operator-roles-matrix.xlsx):
- CA + telemetry certs: we recommend ACME supply a customer-controlled CA for the HSM attestation channel when they have strict custody requirements. Helios can act as a CA only if the customer signs an MOU. We'll add a branch in the matrix for "Customer CA" vs "Helios CA".
- Replication model: prefer wrapped CEKs only. This allows standby regions to remain sealed and eliminates the need to distribute unseal shares. We note risks: longer recovery time if HSM replacement required, but better custody guarantees.
- Operator time-limited tokens: propose using short-lived operator tokens issued by our control-plane through OIDC integration with the customer's IdP; tokens recorded in the audit bundle.

I've added an example rotation workflow in the attached PDF: it shows a canary unwrapping test inside a staging HSM, automated rollback hooks, and a post-rotation attestation captured as a signed artifact.

Questions for ACME (sec-ops@acme.com):
- Do you have an existing CA that must be used for telemetry, or will you accept Helios-managed certs under MOU?
- Are there internal business SLAs for key rotation completion (e.g., <24hrs for emergency rotation)?

Monica
Monica Patel
Manager, Applied Security – Redwood Inference
attachments: operator-roles-matrix.xlsx, rfc-encryption-stewardship-v1.pdf

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Owen Park <owen@helioscloud.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:33:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Encryption stewardship: BYOK operator roles & network isolation RFC

Thanks — matrix looks good to me. A couple minor notes:
- Make the "Custody Operator" process require dual-approval from two different human operators in the on-prem model (we'll use an approver/actor separation).
- Recommend the network diagram include an out-of-band management jump host for emergency operator access and explicit ephemeral egress rules for attestation uploads.

If ACME agrees, I'll update the diagram and push v1.1 of the PDF before the SOC sync. Prefer to keep the first SOC packet minimal: matrix + rotation workflow + network diagram.

Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Security Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, ACME Security <sec-ops@acme.com>, Owen Park <owen@helioscloud.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 16:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Encryption stewardship: BYOK operator roles & network isolation RFC

Thanks everyone for the quick turn. Kimberly here — a couple operational notes from leadership: 
1) Please capture the emergency SLA targets in the RFC and mark which are "customer negotiable" versus "platform guaranteed". Monica, add a small table with three rows: standard rotation, emergency rotation, and recovery-from-HSM-loss turnaround.
2) Once v1.1 of the RFC is ready, route to SOC and Product Compliance. I want a 45-minute review scheduled next week; Ben/Monica/Tessa please propose two 45m slots.
3) For ACME: if you need us to accept an on-prem telemetry collector only, we'll treat that as "no external telemetry" mode and document differences for observability and troubleshooting. That will increase operator friction but preserves custody.

Kimberly Park
VP, Product Security – Redwood Inference
